claims.evidence: The claim is supported by 3D volumetric analysis of post-commissural fornices from cleared whole brains at multiple developmental stages.

claims.claim: In CRMP4-KO mice, the surface area occupied by fibers in the post-commissural fornix progressively decreases in the rostro-caudal region by 30%, 33%, and 47% at three different anatomical planes.
claims.source: In CRMP4-KO mice, the surface area occupied by the fibers in the post-commissural fornix progressively decreased in the rostro-caudal region, by 30%, 33%, and 47% (Figure 5B, C, and D, p = 0.0476, p = 0.0159, p = 0.0159, respectively) compared to the corresponding WT post-commissural fornix.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of gold chloride-stained coronal sections from adult brains at three rostro-caudal planes.

claims.claim: The fornix volume is 31% decreased in Crmp4+/-/Sema3e+/- double mutants compared to WT controls at P0 (p = 0.0061).
claims.source: The fornix volume was 31% decreased in Crmp4+/-/Sema3e+/- double mutants compared to WT controls (Figure 6A and B, p = 0.0061).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by 3D volumetric analysis of segmented fornices from cleared P0 brains of double heterozygous animals.

claims.claim: No significant decrease in fornix volume is observed in Crmp4+/- or Sema3e+/- single mutants (–4% and +2%, p > 0.999 for both).
claims.source: No significant decrease was observed in Crmp4+/- or Sema3e+/- single mutants (Figure 6B, –4% and +2%, p > 0.999 for both).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by 3D volumetric analysis showing no significant difference in fornix volume in single heterozygous animals compared to WT.

claims.claim: CRMP4 interacts with the Sema3E tripartite receptor complex (PlxD1, Nrp1, and VEGFR2).
claims.source: We detected PlxD1, Nrp1, and CRMP4 proteins in VEGFR2 immunoprecipitates, indicating the presence of a complex involving both Sema3E receptor components and CRMP4 (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments in HEK293T/17 cells expressing all four proteins.

claims.claim: CRMP4 interacts with PlxD1 and Nrp1 individually, but not with VEGFR2 alone.
claims.source: VEGFR2 alone did not co-immunoprecipitate with CRMP4-tGFP (Figure 7B), whereas isolated Nrp1 or PlxD1 did (Figure 7C and D). These results strongly suggest that CRMP4 forms a complex with the Sema3E tripartite receptors through interactions with both PlxD1 and Nrp1.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments testing individual receptor-CRMP4 interactions in HEK293T/17 cells.

claims.claim: The interactions between CRMP4 and Sema3E receptors are resistant to concentrations of up to 1% Triton X-100.
claims.source: Indeed, these interactions were even resistant to concentrations of up to 1% Triton X-100 (Figure 8A), suggesting a possible role of DRM domains in their formation.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments performed with different detergent concentrations.

claims.claim: CRMP4, Nrp1, and PlxD1 are found in DRM fractions (PlxD1: 7.7%, Nrp1: 4.3%, CRMP4: 1.6%, flotillin: 53.2%, n = 3).
claims.source: CRMP4, Nrp1, and PlxD1 were also found in the DRM fractions (PlxD1: 7.7%, Nrp1: 4.3%, CRMP4: 1.6%, flotillin: 53.2%, n = 3) but in much lower amounts compared to the membrane fractions (PlxD1: 87.6%, Nrp1: 90.4%, CRMP4: 90.0%, flotillin: 32.4%, n = 3), suggesting that only a small proportion of the Sema3E receptors and CRMP4 locates in DRM (Figure 8B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sucrose-density gradient fractionation experiments of HEK293T/17 cell lysates.

claims.claim: Treatment with 10 mM MβCD for 7 hr results in complete elimination of CRMP4-containing and receptor-containing DRM.
claims.source: Treating cell cultures with 10 mM MβCD for 7 hr resulted in a complete elimination of CRMP4-containing and receptor-containing DRM, and partial reduction of flotillin-containing DRM (Figure 8C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sucrose-density gradient fractionation experiments after MβCD treatment.

claims.claim: The ratio of receptors present in immunoprecipitation relative to CRMP4 is considerably higher in DRM fractions than in RPM fractions (Nrp1 and PlxD1 signals represent 62% and 25% of CRMP4 signal in DRM vs. 0.18% and 0.69% in RPM).
claims.source: Surprisingly, even though the two receptors co-immunoprecipitated with CRMP4 in both RPM and DRM fractions, the ratio of receptors present in the immunoprecipitation relative to the amount of immunoprecipitated CRMP4 was considerably higher in the DRM fraction than in the RPM fraction (Nrp1 and PlxD1 signals represent 62% and 25% of CRMP4 signal, respectively, in DRM fractions, as compared to 0.18% and 0.69% of CRMP4 signal, respectively, in RPM fractions).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments performed on pooled DRM and RPM fractions.

claims.claim: Addition of 1 or 1.5 mM MβCD results in a 1.1-fold increase in axonal length (112% and 115% of control).
claims.source: We first investigated the effect of MβCD on axonal growth, and found, in accordance with previous work (Ko et al., 2005), that the addition of 1 or 1.5 mM of MβCD had a very mild effect, resulting in a 1.1-fold increase in axonal length (Figure 9—figure supplement 1, 112% of control for 1 mM MβCD, and 115% for 1.5 mM).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of axonal length in cultured neurons treated with MβCD and is consistent with previous literature.

claims.claim: Sema3E induces a 1.3-fold increase in axonal length in the absence of MβCD (137% of control, p < 0.0001).
claims.source: Next, Sema3E, in the absence of MβCD, induced an expected 1.3-fold increase in axonal length (Figure 9A and B, 137% of control, p < 0.0001), whereas in the presence of 1.0 and 1.5 mM MβCD, Sema3E no longer stimulated axonal growth (Figure 9A and B, 107% and 101% of control, p = 0.1150 and p > 0.9999, respectively).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of axonal length in cultured subicular neurons treated with Sema3E.

claims.claim: In the presence of 1.0 and 1.5 mM MβCD, Sema3E no longer stimulates axonal growth (107% and 101% of control, p = 0.1150 and p > 0.9999).
claims.source: Next, Sema3E, in the absence of MβCD, induced an expected 1.3-fold increase in axonal length (Figure 9A and B, 137% of control, p < 0.0001), whereas in the presence of 1.0 and 1.5 mM MβCD, Sema3E no longer stimulated axonal growth (Figure 9A and B, 107% and 101% of control, p = 0.1150 and p > 0.9999, respectively).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements showing that MβCD blocks Sema3E-induced axonal growth.

claims.claim: Sema3E treatment triggers an increase in Akt and GSK3β phosphorylation (203% ± 35% and 153% ± 9.5 of control, respectively).
claims.source: As expected, Sema3E treatment triggered the signaling cascade with an increase in Akt and GSK3β phosphorylation (203% ± 35% and 153% ± 9.5 of the control, respectively).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis of phosphorylated Akt and GSK3β in subicular neurons treated with Sema3E.

claims.claim: Sema3E treatment results in a considerable decrease in CRMP4 phosphorylation (43% ± 5.4 of control).
claims.source: In the same experiments, a considerable decrease in CRMP4 phosphorylation (43% ± 5.4 of the control) was observed.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis of phosphorylated CRMP4 in subicular neurons treated with Sema3E.

claims.claim: MβCD treatment inhibits the basal PI3K/AKT pathway (46% ± 15% and 65% ± 12 of control signal for p-AKT and p-GSK3β, respectively).
claims.source: Depleting cholesterol using MβCD (Ohtsuka et al., 2017; Raghu et al., 2010; Scheinman et al., 2013) inhibits the basal PI3k/AKT pathway (46% ± 15% and 65% ± 12 of control signal for p-AKT and p-GSK3β, respectively).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis showing reduced phosphorylation of AKT and GSK3β after MβCD treatment, and is consistent with previous literature.

claims.claim: In the presence of MβCD, application of Sema3E does not lead to increased phosphorylation of p-AKT and p-GSK3β (106% ± 8% and 99% ± 6, respectively), nor to a decrease in CRMP4 phosphorylation (108% ± 8).
claims.source: In the presence of MβCD, the application of Sema3E does not lead to increased phosphorylation of p-AKT and p-GSK3β (106% ± 8% and 99% ± 6, respectively), nor to a decrease in CRMP4 phosphorylation (108% ± 8).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis showing that MβCD blocks Sema3E-induced changes in phosphorylation.

claims.claim: Both CRMP4-4A and CRMP4-4D mutant forms restore axonal growth induced by Sema3E (134% and 141% of control, p < 0.0001 in both cases).
claims.source: Surprisingly, both mutant forms of CRMP4 restored the axonal growth induced by addition of Sema3E (Figure 10B, 134% and 141% of control, respectively, p < 0.0001 in both cases).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments in CRMP4-KO neurons transfected with non-phosphorylatable or phosphomimetic CRMP4 constructs.

claims.claim: CRMP4∆Cyto does not restore Sema3E-induced axonal growth (108% of control, p = 0.1985).
claims.source: CRMP4∆Cyto no longer restored Sema3E-induced axonal growth (Figure 10C, 108% of control, p = 0.1985).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing that CRMP4 lacking the cytoskeleton-binding domain cannot restore Sema3E responsiveness.

claims.claim: CRMP4 is a new specific effector of Sema3E-mediated axonal growth.
claims.source: In this study, we characterized CRMP4 as a new specific effector of Sema3E-mediated axonal growth.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental findings including siRNA knockdown, knockout studies, and rescue experiments demonstrating CRMP4's specific role in Sema3E signaling.

claims.claim: MAP6 acts as a scaffold protein within subicular neurons, facilitating the interaction of Sema3E pathway receptors and downstream SH3-containing actors.
claims.source: We have previously proposed that MAP6 acts as a scaffold protein within subicular neurons, facilitating the interaction of Sema3E pathway receptors and downstream SH3-containing actors (Deloulme et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on previous work by the authors cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: CRMP4-KO mice have defects in fornix development that are identical to those reported in Sema3E-KO mice.
claims.source: In addition, CRMP4-KO mice had defects in fornix development that were identical to those reported in Sema3E-KO mice (Chauvet et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the authors' experimental observations of fornix defects in CRMP4-KO mice and comparison with published data on Sema3E-KO mice.

claims.claim: Crmp4 and Sema3E cooperate to allow the correct establishment of the fornix.
claims.source: Finally, analysis of the fornix in Crmp4/Sema3E double heterozygote animals compared to single heterozygote animals revealed that Crmp4 and Sema3E cooperate to allow the correct establishment of the fornix.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by genetic interaction studies showing fornix defects in double heterozygous animals but not in single heterozygotes.

claims.claim: Sema3A stimulates the development of dendrites in a CRMP4-dependent manner in hippocampal neurons.
claims.source: Thus, Sema3A stimulates the development of dendrites in a CRMP4-dependent manner (Niisato et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Crmp4 and Sema3d genetically interact to promote axonal growth from some peripheral neuron populations in zebrafish.
claims.source: In addition, Crmp4 and Sema3d genetically interact to promote axonal growth from some peripheral neuron populations in zebrafish (Tanaka et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4 share some cellular functions and may have redundant roles related to their extensive sequence homology (74% to 76%).
claims.source: Thus, CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4 share some cellular functions and may have redundant roles that could be related to their extensive sequence homology, which ranges from 74% to 76% (Charrier et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on observations from multiple studies and sequence homology data cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: CRMP4 plays a specific role in the Sema3E signaling pathway.
claims.source: These results suggest that CRMP4 plays a specific role in this signaling pathway.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from experimental results showing that only CRMP4, not CRMP1 or CRMP2, is required for Sema3E signaling.

claims.claim: CRMP4 function is regulated by the molecular context of the neurons where it is expressed.
claims.source: Our research thus contributes to a growing body of work proposing that CRMP4 function is regulated by the molecular context of the neurons where it is expressed (Alabed et al., 2007; Duplan et al., 2010; Girouard et al., 2020; Niisato et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the authors' findings combined with multiple published studies showing context-dependent CRMP4 function.

claims.claim: CRMP4-KO mice display dendritic arborization defects in hippocampal CA1 and cortical pyramidal neurons, mispositioning of Purkinje cells, and olfactory bulb lamination defects.
claims.source: CRMP4-KO mice display dendritic arborization defects in hippocampal CA1 and cortical pyramidal neurons, mispositioning of Purkinje cells, and olfactory bulb lamination defects (Takaya et al., 2017; Tsutiya et al., 2016; Yamazaki et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: A de novo variant of Crmp4 was identified in an adult male with ASD.
claims.source: Moreover, a de novo variant of Crmp4 was recently identified in an adult males with ASD, and CRMP4-KO mice show a decrease in social interaction as well as a severe alterations to their sensory responses (Tsutiya et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: CRMP4-KO mice show a decrease in social interaction and severe alterations to their sensory responses.
claims.source: Moreover, a de novo variant of Crmp4 was recently identified in an adult males with ASD, and CRMP4-KO mice show a decrease in social interaction as well as a severe alterations to their sensory responses (Tsutiya et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Complex formation between CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4, and PlxA1 has been known for several years.
claims.source: Complex formation between CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4, and PlxA1 – a Sema3A co-receptor – has been known for several years (Deo et al., 2004; Schmidt et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: The direct interaction of CRMP2 with PlxA3 is involved in dendritic growth under the control of Sema3A.
claims.source: More recently, a study showed that the direct interaction of CRMP2 with PlxA3 was involved in dendritic growth under the control of Sema3A (Jiang et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Binding of CRMP2 to the Ngr1 receptor and PlxA2 induced by Nogo-A limits axonal regrowth after injury.
claims.source: Binding of CRMP2 to the Ngr1 receptor and PlxA2 induced by Nogo-A was also demonstrated to limit axonal regrowth after injury (Sekine et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: In leukemic T cells, Sema3A/Fas-dependent apoptosis requires Nrp1 and plexin-A1 to co-localize within lipid rafts.
claims.source: For example, in leukemic T cells, Sema3A/Fas-dependent apoptosis requires Nrp1 and plexin-A1 to co-localize within lipid rafts (Moretti et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Lipid rafts are involved in Sema3A-induced growth cone collapse in neurons following the recruitment of Nrp1 to the rafts.
claims.source: Lipid rafts are also involved in Sema3A-induced growth cone collapse in neurons following the recruitment of Nrp1 to the rafts (Guirland et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: The presence of CRMP4 in membrane domains has been implicated in the maintenance of growth cones.
claims.source: The presence of CRMP4 in membrane domains has been implicated in the maintenance of growth cones, suggesting that this localization places CRMP4 in an environment containing specific signaling proteins and cytoskeletal elements (Rosslenbroich et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Cerebral ischemia induced by occlusion leads to CRMP4 and Nrp1 recruitment to lipid rafts.
claims.source: Furthermore, cerebral ischemia induced by occlusion led to CRMP4 and Nrp1 recruitment to lipid rafts, which hints that these molecules play a role in mediating signal transduction in response to neuronal damage triggered by ischemia-reperfusion (Whitehead et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: For particular cellular processes like axonal growth, Akt must localize to regions enriched in sphingolipids and cholesterol.
claims.source: Indeed, for particular cellular processes like axonal growth, Akt must localize to regions enriched in sphingolipids and cholesterol (Gao and Zhang, 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Sema3E's axonal growth-promoting activity relies on the PI3K/Akt pathway, leading to downstream phosphorylation-induced inactivation of GSK3β.
claims.source: Sema3E axonal growth-promoting activity relies on the PI3K/Akt pathway, as it leads to downstream phosphorylation-induced inactivation of GSK3β (Bellon et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Sema3A's repulsive activity is associated with sequential phosphorylation of CRMP2 by Cdk5 and then by GSK3β, blocking interaction between CRMP2 and microtubules in DRG-derived neurons.
claims.source: Conversely, Sema3A's repulsive activity was associated with sequential phosphorylation of CRMP2 by Cdk5 and then by GSK3β, blocking interaction between CRMP2 and microtubules in DRG-derived neurons (Uchida et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: GSK3β-dependent phosphorylation of CRMPs can be considered a mechanism regulating CRMP activity in response to the attractive or repulsive effects of guidance molecules.
claims.source: Therefore, GSK3β-dependent phosphorylation of CRMPs can be considered to be a mechanism regulating CRMP activity in response to the attractive or repulsive effects of the guidance molecules.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of Sema3E and Sema3A signaling mechanisms and their differential effects on CRMP phosphorylation.

claims.claim: CRMP4 phosphorylation may alter its localization rather than its cytoskeleton modulatory function.
claims.source: One explanation for this result could be that CRMP4 phosphorylation alters its localization rather than its cytoskeleton modulatory function. This phosphorylation-dependent localization could have been bypassed following electroporation of CRMP4 plasmids, resulting in ubiquitous overexpression of CRMP4 mutants. This hypothesis has previously been proposed for the response to Sema3D (Tanaka et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: The claim is a speculative explanation for the experimental results, supported by a similar hypothesis from previous literature.

claims.claim: The cytoskeleton-binding domain of CRMP4 is required for Sema3E's growth-promoting activity.
claims.source: Finally, we showed that the cytoskeleton-binding domain of CRMP4 is required for Sema3E's growth-promoting activity, suggesting that CRMP4 plays a role at the interface between Sema3E receptors, located in DRM domains, and the cytoskeleton network.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing that CRMP4 lacking the cytoskeleton-binding domain cannot restore Sema3E responsiveness.

claims.claim: The fornix is affected in many psychiatric diseases, such as schizophrenia.
claims.source: As the fornix is affected in many psychiatric diseases, such as schizophrenia, our results provide new insights to better understand the neurodevelopmental components of these diseases.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about fornix involvement in psychiatric diseases.

claims.claim: The post-commissure of the fornix is the major output of the hippocampus and is mainly composed of subicular axons that primarily terminate in the mammillary bodies.
claims.source: The post-commissure of the fornix is the major output of the hippocampus and is mainly composed of subicular axons that primarily terminate in the mammillary bodies (Witter, 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: The post-commissural fornix belongs to a set of limbic connections, including the Papez circuit, involved in memory, emotion, personality, and navigation.
claims.source: The post-commissural fornix belongs to a set of limbic connections, including the Papez circuit, involved in memory, emotion, personality, and navigation (Bubb et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Disruption of the fornix is associated with several psychiatric disorders and neurodegenerative diseases.
claims.source: Disruption of the fornix is associated with several psychiatric disorders and neurodegenerative diseases (Koshiyama et al., 2020; Nowrangi and Rosenberg, 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: The attractive effect of Sema3E on subicular neurons is crucial for fornix development and is enabled by a tripartite receptor complex composed of PlxD1, Nrp1, and VEGFR2.
claims.source: The attractive effect of Sema3E on subicular neurons is crucial for fornix development and is enabled by a tripartite receptor complex composed of plexin-D1 (PlxD1), neuropilin-1 (Nrp1) and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR2) (Bellon et al., 2010; Chauvet et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Nrp1 has been shown to localize to detergent-resistant membrane (DRM) domains (including lipid rafts).
claims.source: Some receptors involved in semaphorin signaling pathways, such as Nrp1, have been shown to localize to detergent-resistant membrane (DRM) domains (including lipid rafts) (Guirland et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Cholesterol- and sphingolipid-enriched DRM domains are involved in axonal growth and guidance, acting as platforms for ligand-induced receptor activation and recruitment of intracellular actors.
claims.source: Cholesterol- and sphingolipid-enriched DRM domains are involved in axonal growth and guidance, acting as platforms for ligand-induced receptor activation and recruitment of intracellular actors (Simons and Sampaio, 2011).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Kinases downstream of semaphorin signaling, such as Akt or GSK3β, can be recruited to DRM domains where they are activated.
claims.source: For example, kinases downstream of semaphorin signaling, such as Akt or glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK3β), can be recruited to DRM domains where they are activated (Gao and Zhang, 2009; Sui et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: The five CRMPs members have been implicated in numerous neuronal processes including neurite outgrowth, dendritic arborization, axonal regeneration, and axonal transport.
claims.source: The five CRMPs members have been implicated in numerous neuronal processes including neurite outgrowth (Ji et al., 2014; Khazaei et al., 2015), dendritic arborization (Niisato et al., 2012; Niisato et al., 2013), axonal regeneration (Alabed et al., 2007; Alabed et al., 2010; Leung et al., 2002), and axonal transport (Kimura et al., 2005; Tsuboi et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: CRMP2 was the first to be implicated in Sema3A-dependent growth cone collapse in higher vertebrates.
claims.source: Within this family, CRMP2 was the first to be implicated in Sema3A-dependent growth cone collapse in higher vertebrates (Goshima et al., 1995) and continues to be the most extensively studied.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Sema3A stimulates CRMP2 phosphorylation through GSK3β activation which regulates the interaction between CRMP2 and the cytoskeleton.
claims.source: Sema3A stimulates CRMP2 phosphorylation through GSK3β activation which regulates the interaction between CRMP2 and the cytoskeleton (Fukata et al., 2002; Khazaei et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: MAP6 is crucial for fornix development due to its role in regulating axonal elongation induced by Sema3E.
claims.source: Recently, we showed that microtubule-associated protein 6 (MAP6) was crucial for fornix development due to its role in regulating axonal elongation induced by Sema3E (Deloulme et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on previous work by the authors cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: CRMP4 binds the tripartite Sema3E-receptor complex in a DRM domain-dependent manner.
claims.source: The results presented here show that CRMP4 binds the tripartite Sema3E-receptor complex in a DRM domain-dependent manner.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and sucrose gradient fractionation experiments showing preferential interaction in DRM fractions.

claims.claim: Disruption of DRM domains blocks Sema3E-mediated axonal growth and affects CRMP4 phosphorylation by GSK3β.
claims.source: Disruption of DRM domains blocks Sema3E-mediated axonal growth and affects CRMP4 phosphorylation by GSK3β.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experiments showing that MβCD treatment blocks Sema3E-induced axonal growth and prevents changes in CRMP4 phosphorylation.

claims.claim: The integrity of DRM domains is critical for downstream activation of the PI3K/Akt/GSK3β pathway by Sema3E.
claims.source: The integrity of DRM domains is thus critical for downstream activation of the PI3K/Akt/GSK3β pathway by Sema3E.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experiments showing that MβCD treatment blocks Sema3E-induced activation of the Akt/GSK3β pathway.

claims.claim: Sema3E signaling triggers a reduction of GSK3β-driven phosphorylation of CRMP4.
claims.source: Furthermore, we found that Sema3E signaling triggers a reduction of GSK3β-driven phosphorylation of CRMP4, and that the interaction of CRMP4 with the cytoskeleton is necessary to transduce Sema3E signaling.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot analysis showing decreased CRMP4 phosphorylation upon Sema3E treatment.

claims.claim: The interaction of CRMP4 with the cytoskeleton is necessary to transduce Sema3E signaling.
claims.source: Furthermore, we found that Sema3E signaling triggers a reduction of GSK3β-driven phosphorylation of CRMP4, and that the interaction of CRMP4 with the cytoskeleton is necessary to transduce Sema3E signaling.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments showing that CRMP4 lacking the cytoskeleton-binding domain cannot restore Sema3E responsiveness.

claims.claim: CRMP4 is a downstream effector of the Sema3E signaling pathway, exerting its activity through DRM domains and phospho-regulated interactions with the cytoskeleton.
claims.source: Taken together, our results establish CRMP4 as a new specific downstream effector of the Sema3E signaling pathway, exerting its activity through DRM domains and phospho-regulated interactions with the cytoskeleton.
claims.evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on multiple experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claims.claim: DRM/lipid rafts regulate the spatiotemporal recruitment of Sema3E-specific receptors to recruit ubiquitous effectors such as Akt or GSK3β to specific membrane compartments.
claims.source: Our results support the idea that DRM/lipid rafts regulate the spatiotemporal recruitment of Sema3E-specific receptors in order to recruit ubiquitous effectors such as Akt or GSK3β to specific membrane compartments (Averaimo et al., 2016; Lingwood and Simons, 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental results supported by published literature on DRM/lipid raft function.

claims.claim: CRMP4 is the terminal downstream effector of Sema3E in axonal-growth induction, modulating cytoskeletal dynamics to mediate axonal growth.
claims.source: In summary, we propose that CRMP4 is the terminal downstream effector of Sema3E in axonal-growth induction, modulating cytoskeletal dynamics to mediate axonal growth.
claims.evidence: The claim is a proposed model based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claims.claim: The fornix alterations observed in CRMP4-KO mice may contribute to behavioral defects including decreased social interaction and altered sensory responses.
claims.source: It is therefore possible that the fornix alterations we observed in CRMP4-KO mice here may contribute to these behavioral defects.
claims.evidence: The claim is a speculative connection between the anatomical findings and previously reported behavioral phenotypes.

claims.claim: Recent investigations of white matter microstructure by diffusion tensor imaging across psychiatric disorders have highlighted alterations of the fornix in patients suffering from both schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorders (ASD).
claims.source: This tract is crucial for cognitive functions, and in line with this role, recent investigations of white matter microstructure by diffusion tensor imaging across psychiatric disorders have highlighted alterations of the fornix in patients suffering from both schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorders (ASD) (Koshiyama et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on published literature cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Application of Sema3E (5 nM) to WT cultured subicular neurons 48 hr after electroporation with control siRNA induces a 1.2-fold increase in axon length (120%, p < 0.0001).
claims.source: As previously reported (Chauvet et al., 2007; Deloulme et al., 2015), application of Sema3E (5 nM) to WT cultured subicular neurons 48 hr after electroporation with control siRNA induced a 1.2-fold increase in axon length (Figure 2C and D, 120%, p < 0.0001).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements and is consistent with previous literature.

claims.claim: The number of subicular neurons does not differ in adult WT- and CRMP4-KO brains.
claims.source: Readers should note, the number of subicular neurons does not differ in adult WT- and CRMP4-KO brains (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of eYFP-stained subicular neurons in WT and CRMP4-KO brains.

claims.claim: The pre-commissural fornix and medial cortico-hypothalamic tract show no obvious difference between WT and CRMP4-KO mice.
claims.source: Qualitative analysis of the pre-commissural fornix and mcht, using the hybrid uDISCO clearing method (see Materials and method section) on brains expressing YFP across the fornix system, revealed no obvious difference in these tracts between WT and CRMP4-KO mice.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by qualitative analysis of cleared brain images.

claims.claim: The post-commissural projection is the main fornix projection altered in CRMP4-KO.
claims.source: These observations suggest that the post-commissural projection is the main fornix projection altered in CRMP4-KO.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from observations showing defects in the post-commissural fornix but not in other fornix projections.

claims.claim: The defect in fornix development combined with defasciculation observed in CRMP4-KO mice phenotypically copies the defects observed in Sema3E-KO mice.
claims.source: The defect in fornix development combined with defasciculation observed in CRMP4-KO mice phenotypically copies the defects observed in Sema3E-KO mice (Chauvet et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on comparison of the authors' findings with published data on Sema3E-KO mice.

claims.claim: The fornix defects found in single-gene KO and in double heterozygous animals, but not in single heterozygous mice, are strong indicators of an in vivo interaction between Crmp4 and Sema3e during fornix development.
claims.source: The fornix defects found in single-gene KO and in double heterozygous animals, but not in single heterozygous mice, are strong indicators of an in vivo interaction between Crmp4 and Sema3e during fornix development.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from genetic interaction studies showing a specific phenotype in double heterozygotes.

results.result: MAP6 directly interacts with CRMP1, CRMP2, and CRMP4, as identified through immunoaffinity chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry and confirmed by pull-down experiments using purified recombinant proteins.
results.evaluation: Claims C1 and C2 provide converging evidence from both mass spectrometry identification and direct binding assays with purified proteins. The combination of discovery proteomics and biochemical validation with recombinant proteins provides strong support for these direct protein-protein interactions.

results.result: CRMP4, but not CRMP1 or CRMP2, is specifically required for Sema3E-induced axonal growth in cultured subicular neurons, as demonstrated by siRNA knockdown, knockout, and rescue experiments.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C9 and C81 collectively demonstrate CRMP4 specificity through multiple complementary approaches: siRNA knockdown showing only CRMP4 blocks Sema3E response (C5, C6), CRMP4-KO neurons lacking Sema3E responsiveness (C8), and rescue with CRMP4-eGFP restoring function (C9). The statistical significance is reported for all key comparisons, and the consistency across methods strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: CRMP4 is expressed in subicular neurons and their axonal projections during post-commissural fornix formation, with peak expression during embryonic and early postnatal development (E17.5-P7) that declines after P14.
results.evaluation: Claims C10 and C11 are supported by western blot data showing developmental expression patterns and immunolabeling data demonstrating spatial localization. The temporal expression pattern is consistent with the developmental window of fornix formation, and C10 is additionally supported by consistency with prior literature in rat brain.

results.result: CRMP4-KO mice exhibit severe defects in post-commissural fornix development, including reduced diameter (53% at P0), shortened length (26%), decreased volume (40% overall, 51% at P0), and progressive fiber loss in adult brains (30-47% across rostro-caudal planes), while the neighboring mammillo-thalamic tract remains unaffected.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C16 provide comprehensive anatomical characterization using multiple complementary methods (coronal sections, sagittal sections, 3D volumetric analysis, gold chloride staining) across developmental stages and into adulthood. The specificity is demonstrated by the unchanged mammillo-thalamic tract (C13), and all measurements include appropriate statistical analysis with significant p-values. The consistency of defects across methods and developmental stages strongly supports the conclusion.

results.result: Crmp4 and Sema3e genetically interact during fornix development, as demonstrated by a 31% reduction in fornix volume in double heterozygous animals (Crmp4+/-/Sema3e+/-) while single heterozygotes show no defects.
results.evaluation: Claims C17, C18, C37, and C86 demonstrate genetic interaction through the classic approach of examining double heterozygotes. The specific phenotype in double heterozygotes (C17) but not single heterozygotes (C18) is the hallmark of genetic interaction, indicating that the two genes function in the same pathway. The statistical significance (p=0.0061) and appropriate controls support this conclusion.

results.result: CRMP4 interacts with the Sema3E tripartite receptor complex (PlxD1, Nrp1, and VEGFR2) through direct binding to PlxD1 and Nrp1, but not VEGFR2 alone.
results.evaluation: Claims C19 and C20 are supported by systematic co-immunoprecipitation experiments in HEK293T/17 cells. The experiments test both the complete complex (C19) and individual receptor components (C20), demonstrating that CRMP4 binds PlxD1 and Nrp1 but not VEGFR2 alone. This provides clear evidence for the molecular architecture of the complex.

results.result: CRMP4 and Sema3E receptors interact preferentially within detergent-resistant membrane (DRM) domains, with interactions resistant to 1% Triton X-100 and a considerably higher ratio of receptors to CRMP4 in DRM fractions (62% and 25% for Nrp1 and PlxD1) compared to remaining plasma membrane fractions (0.18% and 0.69%).
results.evaluation: Claims C21-C24 and C71 provide multiple lines of evidence for DRM-dependent interactions: detergent resistance (C21), localization to DRM fractions by sucrose gradient (C22), elimination by cholesterol depletion (C23), and enrichment of receptor-CRMP4 complexes in DRM versus RPM fractions (C24). The quantitative data showing dramatic enrichment in DRM fractions strongly supports the conclusion of preferential DRM localization.

results.result: Disruption of DRM domains by methyl-beta-cyclodextrin (MβCD) treatment blocks Sema3E-mediated axonal growth, with Sema3E inducing 1.3-fold axonal growth increase in control conditions but no significant increase in the presence of 1.0-1.5 mM MβCD.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C27 and C72 demonstrate that DRM integrity is required for Sema3E signaling through pharmacological disruption experiments. The mild effect of MβCD alone (C25) contrasts with complete blockade of Sema3E response (C27), indicating specificity. Statistical significance is reported for all comparisons, and the result is consistent with the biochemical data showing DRM-dependent receptor-CRMP4 interactions.

results.result: Sema3E signaling activates the PI3K/Akt/GSK3β pathway and decreases CRMP4 phosphorylation (to 43% of control), and this signaling cascade requires DRM domain integrity, as MβCD treatment blocks both Akt/GSK3β activation and CRMP4 dephosphorylation in response to Sema3E.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C31, C73, and C74 provide comprehensive analysis of the signaling cascade using western blots with phospho-specific antibodies. The data show Sema3E increases Akt and GSK3β phosphorylation while decreasing CRMP4 phosphorylation (C28, C29), and MβCD blocks all these changes (C31). The n=2 for some experiments is relatively low, but the consistency of effects across multiple phosphorylation sites and the clear blockade by MβCD support the conclusions.

results.result: The cytoskeleton-binding domain of CRMP4 is required for Sema3E's growth-promoting activity, as CRMP4ΔCyto fails to rescue Sema3E responsiveness, while both non-phosphorylatable (CRMP4-4A) and phosphomimetic (CRMP4-4D) mutants restore Sema3E-induced axonal growth.
results.evaluation: Claims C32, C33, C58, and C75 demonstrate the importance of the cytoskeleton-binding domain through rescue experiments. The surprising result that both phosphorylation mutants rescue (C32) while the cytoskeleton-binding domain deletion does not (C33) is well-documented with statistical significance. Claim C57 provides a speculative explanation for the phosphorylation mutant results, which is appropriately cautious and supported by prior literature.

results.result: CRMP4 is a specific downstream effector of the Sema3E signaling pathway, functioning through DRM domains and phospho-regulated interactions with the cytoskeleton to modulate axonal growth.
results.evaluation: Claims C34, C41, C76, and C78 represent summary conclusions that integrate multiple experimental findings. These conclusions are well-supported by the collective evidence from knockdown/knockout studies (specificity), biochemical interaction studies (mechanism), DRM localization studies (spatial organization), and rescue experiments (functional validation). The claims appropriately synthesize the major findings of the manuscript.

results.result: CRMP4-KO mice phenotypically copy the fornix defects observed in Sema3E-KO mice, including defasciculation and reduced fornix development.
results.evaluation: Claims C36 and C85 compare the current findings with published data on Sema3E-KO mice. While the authors did not directly compare CRMP4-KO and Sema3E-KO mice side-by-side in this study, the detailed characterization of CRMP4-KO fornix defects (C12-C16) combined with the genetic interaction data (C17-C18) and the cited literature provide reasonable support for this comparison.

results.result: The post-commissural fornix is the main fornix projection altered in CRMP4-KO mice, with no obvious differences in the pre-commissural fornix or medial cortico-hypothalamic tract, and no difference in the number of subicular neurons between WT and CRMP4-KO adult brains.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C84 provide important controls demonstrating specificity of the defect. The quantification of subicular neuron numbers (C82) rules out cell loss as an explanation for the fornix defect. The qualitative analysis of other fornix projections (C83) and the inference about specificity (C84) are appropriately cautious, though C83 notes the analysis was qualitative rather than quantitative.

results.result: MAP6 acts as a scaffold protein within subicular neurons facilitating Sema3E pathway receptor interactions, and is crucial for fornix development through regulating Sema3E-induced axonal elongation.
results.evaluation: Claims C35 and C70 are based on the authors' previous work (Deloulme et al., 2015). These claims provide important context for the current study but represent prior findings rather than new results. The citation is appropriate and the claims are supported by the referenced literature.

results.result: The fornix is affected in psychiatric diseases including schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorders, and the post-commissural fornix is the major hippocampal output composed of subicular axons terminating in mammillary bodies, with Sema3E signaling through PlxD1/Nrp1/VEGFR2 being crucial for its development.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C63 and C80 provide background context from established literature. These are appropriately cited claims that establish the biological and clinical significance of the fornix and the Sema3E signaling pathway. While these are not new findings from this study, they are accurately represented and properly attributed to the cited literature.

results.result: CRMP family members have been implicated in various semaphorin signaling pathways and neuronal processes, with context-dependent functions, and DRM/lipid rafts play established roles in semaphorin signaling and axonal growth through recruitment of receptors and downstream effectors.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C56 and C64-C69 represent literature review and contextualization of the current findings. These claims are appropriately cited and provide important background for interpreting the novel findings. While not new results, they are accurately represented and help establish the conceptual framework for the study.

results.result: DRM/lipid rafts regulate the spatiotemporal recruitment of Sema3E-specific receptors to recruit ubiquitous effectors such as Akt or GSK3β to specific membrane compartments.
results.evaluation: Claim C77 represents an interpretive conclusion that integrates the experimental findings with established concepts from the literature. The claim is supported by the DRM localization data (C21-C24), the functional requirement for DRM integrity (C26-C27, C30-C31), and cited literature on DRM/lipid raft function. This is a reasonable mechanistic interpretation of the data.

results.result: The fornix alterations observed in CRMP4-KO mice may contribute to behavioral defects including decreased social interaction and altered sensory responses previously reported in these mice.
results.evaluation: Claim C79 is explicitly speculative ('it is therefore possible') and connects the anatomical findings to previously reported behavioral phenotypes. While the anatomical defects are well-documented and the behavioral phenotypes are cited from literature, the causal connection between them has not been tested. This represents a reasonable hypothesis for future work but lacks direct experimental support.
